elements.quote: Our living systematic review (LSR) focuses on suicide prevention in relation to COVID-19
elements.reason: The abstract explicitly labels the report as a (living) systematic review.

elements.quote: Our living systematic review (LSR) focuses on suicide prevention in relation to COVID-19, with this iteration synthesising relevant evidence up to June 7th 2020.
elements.reason: The abstract states the review's objective clearly.

elements.quote: Eligibility criteria include incidence/prevalence of suicidal behaviour, exposure-outcome relationships and effects of interventions in relation to the COVID-19 pandemic. Outcomes of interest are suicide, self-harm or attempted suicide and suicidal thoughts. No restrictions are placed on language or study type, except for single-person case reports.
elements.reason: The abstract specifies main inclusion and exclusion criteria.

elements.quote: Method: Automated daily searches feed into a web-based database with screening and data extraction functionalities.
elements.reason: The abstract indicates automated daily searching and a cutoff date ('up to June 7th 2020') but does not name the information sources searched.
The abstract does not mention any risk of bias assessment methods.
The abstract does not describe methods of presenting or synthesizing results (e.g., narrative synthesis, tables, meta-analysis).

elements.quote: Searches identified 2070 articles, 29 (28 studies) met our inclusion criteria, of which 14 articles were research letters or preprints awaiting peer review. All articles reported observational data: 12 cross-sectional; eight case series; five modelling; and three service utilisation studies.
elements.reason: The abstract reports the number of included studies and summarizes study designs, but does not report the total number of participants.

elements.quote: No studies reported on changes in rates of suicidal behaviour. Case series were largely drawn from news reporting in low/middle income countries and factors associated with suicide included fear of infection, social isolation and economic concerns.
elements.reason: The abstract presents results for the main outcomes (suicide, self-harm, suicidal thoughts).

elements.quote: No studies reported on changes in rates of suicidal behaviour.
elements.reason: No meta-analysis was conducted in this iteration of the review, so no summary estimate applies.
No group comparisons with direction of effect are reported in the abstract; no comparative results were identified.

elements.quote: A marked improvement in the quality of design, methods, and reporting in future studies is needed... However, suicide data are challenging to collect in real time and economic effects are evolving.
elements.reason: The abstract summarizes key limitations of the evidence base.

elements.quote: There is thus far no clear evidence of an increase in suicide, self-harm, suicidal behaviour, or suicidal thoughts associated with the pandemic... Our LSR will provide a regular synthesis of the most up-to-date research evidence to guide public health and clinical policy to mitigate the impact of COVID-19 on suicide.
elements.reason: The abstract gives a general interpretation and implications for policy.
The abstract does not mention the funding source for the review.
The abstract does not report the register name (PROSPERO) or registration number.

elements.quote: The COVID-19 pandemic has caused morbidity and mortality, as well as, widespread disruption to people's lives and livelihoods around the world. Given the health and economic threats posed by the pandemic to the global community, there are concerns that rates of suicide and suicidal behaviour may rise during and in its aftermath.
elements.reason: The abstract background describes the current state of knowledge (pandemic's widespread disruption) and the uncertainty (concerns that suicide rates may rise), addressing the existing knowledge context.

elements.quote: Our LSR will provide a regular synthesis of the most up-to-date research evidence to guide public health and clinical policy to mitigate the impact of COVID-19 on suicide.
elements.reason: The need and importance of the review are explained: to provide regular up-to-date synthesis to guide public health and clinical policy during the pandemic.

elements.quote: Details of the living review method, justification for its use and our transition plan are provided in our protocol (John et al ., 2020a).
elements.reason: This is the first iteration of a new living systematic review; no prior similar systematic review is identified in the evidence, so the conditional requirement to justify the review relative to existing similar reviews does not apply.

elements.quote: No studies reported on changes in rates of suicidal behaviour.
elements.reason: Although the review aims also to assess effectiveness of intervention strategies, the review is not primarily a review of intervention effects; no intervention studies were included, so a mechanism-of-action description is not applicable.

elements.quote: All articles reported observational data: 12 cross-sectional; eight case series; five modelling; and three service utilisation studies.
elements.reason: The review is not of complex interventions; all included studies were observational, so a logic model requirement does not apply.

elements.quote: The overarching aim of the review is to identify and appraise any newly published evidence from around the world that assesses the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on suicide deaths, suicidal behaviours, self-harm and suicidal thoughts, or that assesses the effectiveness of strategies to reduce the risk of suicide deaths, suicidal behaviours, self-harm and suicidal thoughts, resulting from the COVID-19 pandemic.
elements.reason: The review objectives are explicitly stated in an 'Aim' section, specifying populations/outcomes (suicide deaths, suicidal behaviours, self-harm, suicidal thoughts) and the exposures/interventions of interest, and are further operationalised as explicit research questions in text_8 ('Studies must address one of the following research questions...').

elements.quote: Eligibility criteria include incidence/prevalence of suicidal behaviour, exposure-outcome relationships and effects of interventions in relation to the COVID-19 pandemic.
elements.reason: Planned comparisons are implied (prevalence during vs not during pandemic, impact of exposures and intervention effects; text_8 lists comparative prevalence/incidence questions), but no formal PICO-formulated statement of planned comparisons for intervention effects is provided.

elements.quote: Study participants may be adults or children of any ethnicities living in any country. Outcomes of interest are: Deaths by suicide Self-harm ... or attempted suicide ... Suicidal thoughts/ideation ... Studies must address one of the following research questions: (i) What is the prevalence/incidence? ... (ii) What is the comparative prevalence/incidence?
elements.reason: Eligibility section specifies populations (any age, ethnicity, country), outcomes, and the research questions studies must address; study designs are unrestricted except single-person case reports (text_3, callout_0).

elements.quote: There was no restriction on language of publication. ... Pre-prints were re-assessed at the time of publication and most current version included.
elements.reason: Report characteristics covered: no language restriction, preprints included and re-assessed; date range of searching (1 Jan 2020 to 7 June 2020) also stated.
No evidence distinguishes exclusion for outcomes not measured versus outcomes not reported.

elements.quote: Results were synthesised separately for studies in the general population, in health and social care staff and other at-risk occupations, and in vulnerable populations (e.g. people of older age or those with underlying conditions...).
elements.reason: Synthesis groups are specified and linked to the research questions/themes defined in the eligibility criteria.

elements.quote: We did not include Google Trends studies ... since search data constitute a proxy measure but findings are largely mixed. We also excluded grey literature (Fancourt & Steptoe, 2020).
elements.reason: Rationale given for excluding Google Trends studies, but no rationale is provided for the notable exclusion of single-person case reports or grey literature.

elements.quote: A sample search strategy (for PubMed) appears in Box 1 from 1 st Jan 2020 to June 7 th 2020. ... For this version of the living review, Psy- and SocArXiv searches were carried out retrospectively on the 12 th of June, using a publication date filter for Jan 1 st 2020 - June 7 th 2020.
elements.reason: Dates are given for the PubMed sample search and the PsyArXiv/SocArXiv searches, and daily automated searching is described, but an explicit last-searched date is not stated for every individual source (e.g., Scopus, WHO, CORD-19).

elements.quote: We searched the following electronic databases: PubMed; Scopus; medRxiv, bioRxiv; the COVID-19 Open Research Dataset (CORD-19) by Semantic Scholar and the Allen Institute for AI, which includes relevant records from Microsoft Academic, Elsevier, arXiv and PMC; and the WHO COVID-19 database. ... Searches are conducted daily via PubMed and Scopus application programme interface and the bioRxiv and medRxiv RSS feeds.
elements.reason: Database names are given and access methods (APIs, RSS feeds) are described, but coverage dates of the databases are not reported; date restrictions are given only in the sample PubMed search.

elements.quote: the COVID-19 Open Research Dataset (CORD-19) ... and the WHO COVID-19 database. ... We therefore included PsyArXiv and SocArXiv repositories in our search strategy via their own open access platforms
elements.reason: Registers/repositories (CORD-19, WHO database, PsyArXiv, SocArXiv) are named with date filters for PsyArXiv/SocArXiv, but date restrictions are not reported for all registers (e.g., WHO, CORD-19).

No individuals were reported as contacted to identify studies.

elements.quote: A sample search strategy (for PubMed) appears in Box 1 from 1 st Jan 2020 to June 7 th 2020. ... Search.docx (additional information about the searches, including full search strategies)
elements.reason: A full PubMed search strategy is reported in Box 1, but strategies for the other databases (Scopus, WHO, CORD-19, preprint repositories) are not reported in the manuscript itself; only a pointer to extended data with full search strategies is given, so complete strategies for every source are not presented in the text.

elements.quote: No restrictions were placed on the types of study design eligible for inclusion, except for the exclusion of single-person case reports. ... There was no restriction on language of publication. ... using a publication date filter for Jan 1 st 2020 - June 7 th 2020.

elements.quote: A two-stage screening process was undertaken to identify studies meeting the eligibility criteria. First, two authors (either CO or EE) assessed citations from the searches and identified potentially relevant titles and abstracts. Second, either DG, AJ or RW assessed the full texts of potentially eligible studies
elements.reason: Number of reviewers is reported for each stage: two authors screened titles/abstracts and one author assessed full texts.

elements.quote: First, two authors (either CO or EE) assessed citations from the searches and identified potentially relevant titles and abstracts.

elements.quote: the following basic data were extracted: citation; study aims and objectives; country/setting; characteristics of participants; methods; outcome measures (related to self-harm / suicidal behaviour and COVID-19); key findings; strengths and limitations; reviewer's notes.
